target_customer: Teams and small businesses that want AI agents to own recurring back office and knowledge work across their tools
problem: Chatbots answer questions but do not do work or keep running. Tasklet agents connect to many tools, take actions, and run in the cloud on triggers.
business_model: Usage-based credits per organization, free to start, paid plans from $25 per month, no per-seat fee
product_category: AI agent platform for business automation

founders.name: Andrew Lee
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page; education not listed.

founders.name: Jonny Dimond
founders.background_notes: Early Firebase team member and technical lead for Cloud Firestore per the YC page.

competitors.name: Zapier
competitors.what: Rule-based workflow automation with large integration library
competitors.traction_then: incumbent with very large user base

technical_complexity.rationale: Cloud agent runtime, sandboxed code execution, browser use, and a connections layer are substantial but built on frontier models and MCP; the team had prior experience building an AI agent inside Shortwave.

defensibility.rationale: Agents holding long-running workflows and connections create some lock-in, but model access and agent frameworks are widely available and many rivals exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents added AI agent features, but Tasklet raised $20M in April 2026 and a further round in October 2026 and remains independent.

market_need_then: Knowledge workers juggle many SaaS apps manually; the October 2025 launch followed Shortwave users asking for the agent as a standalone product, and a Sacra estimate (third party) put growth from under $1M to about $10M ARR in roughly five months.

identity.logo: Wordmark; a brand page exists but was not read
identity.visual_style: Clean light layout with short action headlines

branding.community_and_virality: Covered on The New Stack, the Cognitive Revolution podcast, Product Hunt and Sacra; the site lists customer logos and stories.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear descriptive-feeling name and steady press and podcast coverage helped by the founder's Firebase record, but no distinctive mascot or signature asset found.

pivots.from: AI agent feature inside the Shortwave email client
pivots.why: Users asked for the agent without the email app per the founders' launch post; sources differ on exact spin-out timing

outcome_analysis: Tasklet grew out of Shortwave's agent work, launched standalone in October 2025, and raised $20M in April 2026 at a reported $175M valuation, then about $12.8M in October 2026. Experienced repeat founders, rapid revenue growth claims and a timing tailwind from capable models drive the story; risks are intense competition from automation incumbents and agent platforms and thin defensibility.
notes: Round stage labels are not stated by the company blog, so recorded as other (seedtable calls the April round Series A and Dealroom calls the later one a bridge). The October round amount is from one outlet and a second report of about $13M by Dealroom; a $500M valuation appears on the careers page and one outlet but is not recorded as a post-money. Total raised claims vary ($20M, $29.5M, over $42M). Education for Lee not listed.
